title: Chain Rule on a Nested Power
subtitle: Differentiating sine cubed of a linear input

problem.prompt: Differentiate the function using the chain rule, then evaluate the derivative at the given point. Give the exact value.

equations.title: Chain rule
equations.text: Here f is the outer function and g is the inner function. The outer derivative is evaluated at the unchanged inner expression, then multiplied by the inner derivative.

equations.title: Three-layer chain rule
equations.text: With u the outer input, v the middle input, and x the variable, each nesting level contributes one derivative factor.

equations.title: Power rule
equations.text: Used for the outer cube, with n equal to three and u equal to sine of two x.

equations.title: Derivative of sine
equations.text: Valid when v is measured in radians. The argument is carried through unchanged.

equations.title: Linear inner function
equations.text: A linear inner layer contributes only the constant a, which here equals two.

equations.title: Power reducing identity for sine cubed
equations.text: Used only as an independent verification route with theta equal to two x.
